items.quote: else -- neighbouring entrances across a cluster border
items.what: When two consecutive hops share a cluster (ka == kb) but the refining grid search fails, the else branch still runs and adds just the two entrance nodes, so the walk is drawn as a straight segment between them with no reason surfaced; the comment also only describes the cross-border case
items.why: The abstract A* already accepted the hop and returned its cost, so the callback receives a normal points/cost result whose drawn segment may cross walls, not a Path failure reason. Reaching it needs a baked intra-cluster edge that the decoded grid cannot walk (baker/runtime mismatch), which is rare; either split the branches so the ka == kb failure is surfaced (or at least logged in the debug trace), or state in the comment that the straight fallback is intended
items.reason: gen_nav.py:grid_hpa creates intra-cluster edges only between reachable nodes, and runtime searches verified all 720,486 shipped directed intra-cluster edges across all three maps are reachable. The alleged failure requires a separate, unestablished violation of that generated-data invariant.

items.quote: local function run(map, from, to, waterWalking, costOnly)
items.what: run (355-580, 225 lines) holds endpoint resolution and snapping (356-378), the cached abstract A* (379-482), hop refinement into grid nodes with loop cutting (490-550), and smoothing into world points with wet yards (552-579).
items.why: The stated reason (line 354: A* and refinement share scratch trees) does not bind: the trees are module upvalues (trees, ag/apar/...) swapped by scratch(), not run's locals. Refinement and point building run once per search after the A* loop, so Refine(st, hops, ...) and Points(st, P, keep, from, to) could be separate functions without adding calls to the expansion loop. Low: the file is under the size rule and the function is coherent as one search pipeline.
items.reason: The coherent-responsibility exclusion applies: run constructs one HPA* result, with refinement consuming the selected endpoint surfaces and cached hops; smoothing is already delegated to PathGrid.lua. Independently, commit 528cfe2 localized its loop-cutting change to the existing add helper, and both path specs pass; possible extraction alone does not establish an oversized-function defect.

items.quote:
if ka == kb and search(st, ka, swim, ea, R, eb) then
local nodes = trace(R, eb, {})
addAll(ka, nodes, #nodes, 1, -1)
else -- neighbouring entrances across a cluster border
items.what: A same-cluster abstract hop (ka == kb) whose grid search fails falls into the cross-border branch and is refined as two bare entrance points, i.e. a straight segment between entrances anywhere in the cluster.
items.why: The else is written (and commented) for adjacent entrances across a cluster border; for ka == kb the baked graph says the entrances connect, so a failed search means graph/grid disagreement (e.g. evicted or mismatched data). The route is still returned with the graph cost and the drawn walk cuts straight through the cluster, with no reason or log. Separating the ka == kb failure (error or 'unreachable') from the border case would surface it. Cannot prove the failure is reachable with shipped data, hence medium.

items.quote: for e = 1, B64[byte(s, 9 + (id % 4096) * 7)] do
items.what: The graph node-record layout (header n(2), then 7-char records cell(3) layer(1) component(2) degree(1)) is restated as independent magic offsets in three places: decodeGraph (PathGrid.lua:500-508, pos = 3, pos + 6, pos + 7), metadata (528-529, 3 + (id % 4096) * 7, pos + 3, pos + 4) and adjacent (541, the precomputed 9 + i * 7 for the degree byte). Canonical home: metadata's record position (one RECORD = 7 / header offset), with adjacent reusing it (pos + 6).
items.why: The encoder is the spec: tools/baker/gen_nav.py:677-679 writes enc(len, 2) then enc(cell,3)+enc(layer,1)+enc(comp,2)+enc(degree,1), documented in the generated header (gen_nav.py:738-739). Cross-language restatement in the decoder is unavoidable; the intra-file restatement is not: '9' folds header + degree offset into one literal that no longer reads as either, so a record-width or header change to the encoder must be found in three decoder sites. Not a hot-loop inline: adjacent decodes once per entrance and caches (549).
items.reason: Not a verdict on the defect: the file moved to Routing/PathGrid.lua in the module reorganisation, and the item is carried forward as eda635f6ea.

items.quote: ---@param callback fun(cost: number?, reason: string?, job: SPFPathJob)
items.what: Walk failure reasons are a closed set ("nodata", "outside", "offmesh", "unreachable", "error") passed as bare strings typed `string`: produced at Path.lua:358, 368, 372, 410, 469, 594 (failed("nodata")), 271/274 (pointNode), PathJobs.lua:74 ("error"), Corpse.lua:68, 70 and Journey.lua:415; compared by literal at JourneyCosts.lua:222, 289, 291, 329; mapped in ns.WalkFailure (JourneySteps.lua:20-26); listed in prose at PathJobs.lua:125. A typo such as "off-mesh" at a producer or JourneyCosts.lua:329 comparison type-checks and silently falls through WalkFailure to the generic 'walking search failed'. The project profile lists exactly this ('Path failure reasons (Journey.lua WALK_FAILURE)') under Anti-patterns. items.quote: function Planner.Plan(options)
items.what: Planner.Plan is 433 lines (321-754) with five separable stages: topology cache check and build (322-484), per-plan dynamic edges for ride/teleports/walk pairs (486-532), backward Dijkstra lower bound (536-570), the bounded label search (571-698), and leg reconstruction/flight merging (699-754).
items.why: The stated reason (line 320: splitting adds hot-path upvalues) covers the label search and its heap only. The topology build runs on a cache miss, the lower bound is a pure function of edges and goal, and leg reconstruction runs once per plan over labels/nodes; extracting BuildTopology(options), LowerBounds(edges, goal, ...) and Legs(labels, nodes, finishAt) adds no call inside the search loop. Proposal only; the split must keep the 3 ms benchmark (AGF_BENCH/journey_bench) unchanged.

items.quote: "revision",
items.what: test-only: the `revision` topology cache key (and the 'or advancing revision' clause of the comment above CACHE_KEYS) is set by no production caller; delete it with tests/runtime_spec.lua lines 63-64 (`options.revision = 1` / compare()) and the `---@field revision? number` on SPFPlanOptions in types/Addon.lua:226
items.why: Only two production callers pass `cache` to Planner.Plan: Journey.lua Plan (options table at 667-688) and API.lua Options (152-171); neither sets `revision`. tools/bake_walks.lua loads Planner but never calls Plan with a cache. rg 'revision' over all .lua finds only tests/runtime_spec.lua:63 as a setter; other hits are unrelated (Arrow local, PathJobs job.revision, Route geometry revision, SPFPathJob type). Same result via git grep on all six in-flight branches. Hard stops: not string-built (CACHE_KEYS is a literal list read by ipairs), not persisted (topology lives in a per-session cache table), not wire/public (API.Estimate builds its own options; external callers cannot pass options), no non-source caller. Without the key a spec that swaps data tables still invalidates via the identity-compared data keys.

items.quote: function Planner.QuestDestination(questID, title, complete, uiMapID, pois, waypoint)
items.what: Routing/Planner.lua (833 lines against a 1000-line gate) holds four responsibilities: picking a quest's destination from native POIs (:19-58, needs the locale table), leg drawing geometry (:60-148, WalkPoints, WalkContradicts, LegPoints), the fixed places and their baked-walk keys (:150-275), and the label search itself (:277-833).
items.why: The first two never change with the search: QuestDestination's only runtime caller is Journey/JourneyInput.lua:36 and it is the reason this file loads ns.L; LegPoints is called from UI/Route.lua:525, UI/RouteTransports.lua:117 and Core/PlanContext.lua:111. They sit here as pure functions for planner_spec. QuestDestination would live in Journey/JourneyInput.lua and the geometry in its own file next to PlanContext, leaving Planner with places and search. Plan itself is one 500-line function (:332-831) with a stated hot-path reason for not splitting, so it is not part of this finding.
items.reason: Split this along the named seams, and into which files? Defect: Routing/Planner.lua (833 lines against a 1000-line gate) holds four responsibilities: picking a quest's destination from native POIs (:19-58, needs the locale table), leg drawing geometry (:60-148, WalkPoints, WalkContradicts, LegPoints), the fixed places and their baked-walk keys (:150-275), and the label search itself (:277-833). Evidence: JourneyInput.lua consumes QuestDestination to interpret native quest POIs, while PlanContext.lua and the route UI consume LegPoints for drawing, independently of the topology and label search. Quest selection and leg geometry separate cleanly from places and planning, but choosing and moving those module boundaries requires a reviewed design change.

items.what: Sync re-parses the route ID out of Model.Encode's formatted "<route>:<seen>:<phase>" strings to key them by route, restating Model's entry format (Model.lua:172-183) outside its owner; Model.Encode then sorts a list whose order Sync discards by rekeying into a hash (Flush iterates with pairs).

items.quote: local uiMap = GetTaxiMapID and GetTaxiMapID()
items.what: Existence guard on GetTaxiMapID, a global API present in every client flavor (Ketho's pinned annotations, src/data/flavor.ts: `["GetTaxiMapID"]: 0xF`), and called only while a flight master's map is open.
items.why: The same file calls NumTaxiNodes, TaxiNodeGetType, GetNumRoutes and TaxiGetNodeSlot unguarded; the specs (taxi_spec, ui_client) stub GetTaxiMapID. With the guard removed all specs, UI checks and typecheck pass. If the API were ever missing, the guard would silently leave every character with no known flight points (the planner then never flies) instead of erroring. Use `local uiMap = GetTaxiMapID()`.

items.quote: t = math.max(0, math.min(1, ((x - a.x) * dx + (y - a.y) * dy) / length ^ 2))
items.what: Tracker's JourneyDistance projects the player onto each leg's points to get yards remaining (Tracker.lua:129-148), a third copy of ns.OnWalk (Journey.lua:295-317; canonical) and Arrow.lua:109-120.
items.why: Differences: Tracker caches per-leg lengths/after (intentional, avoids recomputation per tick), has no off-path reach limit, applies it to active boat/flight legs as well as walks, and adds the off-path distance only for walks (intentional). The projection/after arithmetic itself is identical and would need the same fix in each copy; OnWalk could take precomputed lengths, or expose the projection as a shared helper.
items.reason: These serve different contracts: Tracker caches discontinuous, multimodal geometry, excludes jumps and continent gaps, and adds off-path distance only for walks; tests/tracker_ui.lua:98–106 requires those exclusions, and executing the unchanged functions produced 200 yards versus OnWalk’s 1000 for the jump fixture. OnWalk instead supplies reach-limited walking progress, while Arrow selects a bend without calculating remaining yards; the shared clamped projection is a small mathematical idiom, covered by the lens’s exclusions.
